signals.title: USD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Fed-SNB Carry
signals.text: The USD/CHF pair at 0.8007 represents the most extreme divergence in the G10 scorecard, with the USD lagging its peers by -1.038% while CHF leads at +0.805%. This 1.842% weekly spread develops despite a massive +375bp nominal carry advantage for the USD, as Fed 3.75% vs SNB 0.00% fails to attract buyers amidst broader USD weakness. Technically, the pair is trading below its SMA20 at 0.8112 and SMA50 at 0.8081, confirming a strong bearish momentum that ignores the carry premium. While US Treasury buyback news has introduced volatility, the USD remains under pressure as the market digests recent yield shifts and Treasury auction results. Trade bias: Bearish USD/CHF; bearish momentum overrides the structural carry advantage. Catalyst: next SNB meeting — hold priced. Risk: DXY recovers back toward the SMA20/50 cluster near 100.14, signaling a broad USD reversal.

signals.title: NZD/USD — ESI + RBNZ Hike Bias
signals.text: NZD/USD at 0.5944 shows strong bullish momentum, advancing for a second consecutive day as RBNZ rate hike expectations strengthen ahead of the September 2nd meeting. The NZD ESI index at +12.6 confirms that domestic data is outperforming expectations, providing a fundamental tailwind even as COT LF net short of -34,031 (pctl 2, z -2.00) remains at extreme levels. This positioning creates a significant short-squeeze risk, as specs are caught short against a hawkish RBNZ policy bias and improving macro data. The pair is holding firmly above its SMA200 at 0.5838, which now acts as a structural floor for the move higher. Trade bias: Bullish NZD/USD; extreme spec shorts face a squeeze on hawkish RBNZ pricing. Catalyst: RBNZ meeting 2 Sep — hike priced. Risk: RBNZ pivot to a hold stance removes the squeeze catalyst.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew + Vol Divergence
signals.text: USD/JPY at 159.13 is exhibiting a notable divergence between spot price action and the options market, with the 25d risk reversal (RR) showing a strong put skew of -2.02. This extreme options demand for downside protection coincides with a negative VRP of -1.2%, where ATM IV at 7.2% sits below realized vol of 8.4%, suggesting a market that is underpricing potential volatility shocks despite paying for downside tails. While the +275bp Fed-BoJ carry differential remains the primary driver for spot bids, the options market is clearly hedging for a sharp reversal ahead of Japanese CPI data. The pair remains technically vulnerable while trading below its SMA20 (159.91) and SMA50 (161.03) clusters. Trade bias: Neutral USD/JPY; options skew signals heavy hedging against the carry-trade consensus. Catalyst: Japan CPI release Friday Aug 21. Risk: Strong CPI print triggers a disorderly carry unwind through the SMA200 at 158.28.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Retail Divergence + Technical Resistance
signals.text: AUD/USD at 0.7114 is currently facing a retail sentiment extreme, with 85% of retail traders holding short positions. This retail bias directly diverges from COT LF positioning, which is net long +45,727, suggesting institutional players are comfortably positioned for further upside while retail fades the move. The pair is supported by a -70bp carry premium in favor of the AUD (SOFR 3.65% vs AONIA 4.35%), and price action remains constructive above the SMA20 at 0.7041. While ESI remains moderately negative at -10.3, the technical structure and institutional-retail divergence support a 'buy-the-dip' regime. Trade bias: Bullish AUD/USD, contrarian to retail extreme. Catalyst: Australian Flash PMI data release. Risk: A break below the SMA50 at 0.6999 invalidates the immediate bullish structure.
